# Source notices

The AWS model bytes are copied from `aws/api-models-aws` at the immutable commit named in `manifest.json`. Its exact `LICENSE` is retained at `official/aws/LICENSE`; preserve its notices with any redistribution or derivative use.

Google Discovery documents are obtained from the public Discovery endpoints named in `manifest.json`. The Discovery service describes the machine-readable metadata as API methods, schemas and OAuth scopes. Its service terms incorporate the Google APIs Terms of Service: [Discovery terms](https://developers.google.com/discovery/terms), [Google APIs Terms](https://developers.google.com/terms/). Documentation pages state CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted, but that statement does not by itself license every API payload for redistribution. This testdata is internal, contains no customer data, and must receive a licensing review before wider redistribution.

The synthetic fixtures are authored examples. They are not copied customer responses, do not contain object contents, and are not provider documentation or qualified source evidence.

The lifecycle pages under `official/lifecycle/` are exact public primary-source captures identified and hash-bound by `lifecycle-evidence.json`. They are retained only for internal offline evidence tests; the observations remain unqualified candidates and must not be redistributed without an applicable licensing review.

The unit page under `official/units/` is likewise an exact public primary-source capture identified by `unit-evidence.json`. Its GiB observation is deliberately scoped to the cited Compute Engine disk case and is not a field-name-based unit rule.

The EC2 volume and Compute Engine lifecycle captures added for the version-2 mappings are exact primary-source evidence, byte-bound by their case mappings. `native-source-snapshots.json` distinguishes immutable repository copies from the original provider capture identities; a repository snapshot does not authenticate a provider capture or qualify a semantic interpretation.
